tags: [fermentation, hot-sauce, truck]

Fermented mash log. House sauce is "Levvy Red", bottled 150 ml at £6. Mash ratio is always 3% salt by total weight (chillies + aromatics), no added water.

- **2024-06-08** Batch HS-01. 1 kg Scotch bonnets from the Caribbean grocer on Stockport Road, £9. Stems off, seeds in. 200 g carrot, 100 g garlic. Total 1.3 kg, so 39 g salt. Blitzed coarse in the Robot Coupe, packed into a 2 L jar, glass weight, airlock lid ([[Fermentation weights and airlocks]]). Gloves. Wear gloves.
- **2024-06-11** Bubbling hard, airlock going every few seconds. 23°C.
- **2024-06-20** pH 3.6. Smells fruity and funky. Tasted: wow.
- **2024-07-06** 4 weeks. pH 3.4. Blended with 250 ml cider vinegar and 40 g of the Heaton Moor honey from mum's neighbour (the one who did the [[Honey extraction day]] write-up). Strained through a chinois. Yield 1.1 L, 7 bottles. Sold out in a weekend.
- **2024-08-03** HS-02. Doubled: 2 kg bonnets, 400 g red pepper for body, 150 g garlic, 2.55 kg total, 77 g salt. 3 L jar.
- **2024-08-09** White film on top. Kahm, not mould. Skimmed. Lesson: more weight, less headspace.
- **2024-09-14** HS-02 bottled. 22 bottles. Added 2 g xanthan per litre so it doesn't separate in the bottle. Worth it.
- **2024-10-19** HS-03, smoked version. 600 g dried chipotle morita and 400 g guajillo rehydrated, plus 500 g fresh jalapeño. Chillies from the Mexican shop online (Cool Chile Co, £22). Idea came from the salsa notes in [[Viaje a Oaxaca]].
- **2024-11-30** HS-03 at 6 weeks, pH 3.5. Smoky, deep, less heat. Code HS-03S, £6.50.
- **2025-03-15** HS-04. Back to bonnets, 3 kg. 4% salt this time because it's going to sit 3 months. Expect slower.
- **2025-06-21** HS-04 opened at 14 weeks. Best one yet. Also using a spoon of it in the duck sauce on the truck.

Totals so far: 4 batches, 7.85 kg raw chillies, 74 bottles, cost about £1.40 a bottle.
